setup: Ball of one foot on the edge of a step
Heel free to drop below the step
Hold a rail or wall lightly for balance
Other foot lifted or hooked behind
execution: Rise as high as you can onto the ball of your foot
Lower slowly until your heel is below the step
Keep your knee straight but not locked
faults: Don't push yourself up with your hand
Don't let your ankle roll outward

notes: Use the rail or wall for balance only, so the calf does the work and you stay steady.
Use a stable step with a non-slip edge. If your foot slides, step down rather than catching yourself on one leg.
To add load, hold a dumbbell on the working side and log it as added weight.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

regressions.name: Calf raise (bodyweight)
regressions.reason: Both legs share the load; learn the full range first.

regressions.name: Single-leg calf raise on flat ground
regressions.reason: No step, so a shorter range and easier balance.

progressions.name: Single-leg calf raise with a dumbbell
progressions.reason: Hold a dumbbell on the working side; log it as added weight.

progressions.name: Slower lowering
progressions.reason: Take about three seconds to lower each rep.

substitutions.name: Leg-press calf raise
substitutions.reason: Calves only, with the back supported.

substitutions.name: Seated calf raise
substitutions.reason: Bent knees shift more work to the lower calf.

substitutions.name: Standing barbell calf raise
substitutions.reason: Both legs with a barbell in a rack.

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view at knee height, figure facing right, standing on one foot on a step with a hand on a wall or rail. The ankle and the heel's travel below the step must be clear.

keyPositions.label: Bottom
keyPositions.describe: Standing tall on one foot, ball of the foot on the step's edge, heel dropped below it for a calf stretch. Knee straight but soft; other foot lifted behind. One hand lightly on the wall.

keyPositions.label: Top
keyPositions.describe: Heel raised as high as possible over the ball of the foot. Body rises straight up as one piece; knee unchanged; hand still only resting.

ikHints: Ball of the standing foot fixed on the step edge
Hand rests on the wall without pushing
emphasise: Heel drops below the step, then rises high

sources.title: Hébert-Losier K et al. (2017) Updated reliability and normative values for the standing heel-rise test in healthy adults. Physiotherapy 103(4):446-452
sources.supports: Context: single-leg heel rises to fatigue are a reliable, standard calf test with published norms (566 adults); cues.execution[0,2]
